    Cryptography, Explained

    A plain-English, one-stop guide to how secrets are kept, from Caesar's cipher to post-quantum TLS

    Every secret on the internet is guarded by math. Let’s learn how.

    ▶ Start the journey⚡ 60-second Shorts

    22 chapters · 80 interactive demos (many running real crypto) · 150+ pros & cons cards · 1 locked vault

    You use cryptography hundreds of times a day without noticing. Unlocking your phone, sending a WhatsApp message, paying with a card, loading any website with a padlock, connecting to Wi-Fi, installing an app update: every one of these depends on cryptography.

    This guide explains how all of it works, in everyday language. You don't need a math degree or a programming background. When math helps, you'll get a short "Math corner" with the intuition and no proofs. When networking matters (and for internet security it often does), you'll get a "Networking primer" that explains just enough.

    By the end you should be able to:

    • Explain encryption, hashing, signatures and key exchange to a friend.
    • Understand what actually happens when your browser shows a padlock.
    • Create your own certificate authority and issue certificates with it.
    • Read terms like TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 or X25519MLKEM768 and know what each part means.
    • Spot common crypto mistakes and know which algorithms to use (and avoid) today.
    🔒

    The mystery

    A secret message is locked in this vault

    It’s encrypted with real AES-256-GCM. The key is stretched with PBKDF2 from 22 words. Beat each chapter’s boss quiz to earn one word. Collect all 22 and the vault opens.
